title: Bound one-shear physical fiber Lp uniformly in action and static calibration
statement: For nonzero transverse fiber beta>=1, repaired future Jost coefficients Q1(n)=sum_(m>=n+1)c_m and Qr(n)=Q_(r-1)(n+1)+sum_(m>=n+1)c_m Q_(r-1)(m+1) are positive and decreasing in n. Their normalized total coefficient mass is <=exp(42), uniformly in beta. Positive mixtures of finite-interval and half-line Fourier projections give physical-circle Jost synthesis and adjoints <=p_exp exp(42), p_exp>=2. Full-circle scattering reconstructs same-half blocks symmetrically, avoiding triangular truncation; spectral norm/form excludes omitted point modes. Native polarization multipliers have uniform bounded variation. Thus each physical longitudinal velocity fiber has Lp norm <=2^200 p_exp^4, independent of action/direction/phase; the zero fiber is unchanged. H3 transverse summation gives ||U f||Lp(T3)<=2^256 p_exp^4||f||H3. A source corollary gives a [1+log(2+2^29|s|)]^4 physical-supnorm envelope. This is not a full 3D Lp-to-Lp or viscous-semigroup theorem. The completed end-to-end review substantively rechecks this sensitive physical-space argument.
